_about: Corrections to base.jsonl established by the research entries (2026-10-12). Keys: date, title, summary, states (replace); date_note / title_note (add a note without changing the value); why (source). Applied by pipeline/build_dataset.py.

proc-796.why: The signed original and the Statutes' margin date (35 Stat. 2177) give January 16, 1908; the printed dating clause on p. 2178 reads "twenty-eighth", a misprint repeated in later lists.

proc-579.why: Statutes margin and dating clause read "this 14th day of July" (34 Stat. 3113).

proc-776.why: Statutes margin and dating clause read "this twenty-fifth day of October" (35 Stat. 2156); the 26th is the day the text reached the press.

proc-818.date_note: Some sources date this July 1, 1908; the Statutes at Large print it under July 2 (35 Stat. 2196). Check the signed original.

proc-814.title: Enlarging the Grand Canyon National Game Preserve, Arizona
proc-814.title_note: The American Presidency Project and the Statutes list caption this "Setting aside the Grand Canyon National Game Preserve"; the proclamation enlarged the preserve created in 1906.
proc-814.why: Working notes removed from the title; 35 Stat. 2192.

proc-801.title: Diminishing Lincoln National Forest, New Mexico
proc-801.title_note: The American Presidency Project and the printed list of proclamations say "Lincoln National Monument", an error: the document concerns the Lincoln National Forest.

proc-813.title: Announcing the Death of Ex-President Grover Cleveland
proc-813.why: Working notes removed from the title; 35 Stat. 2193.

proc-807.title: Setting aside Lewis and Clark Cavern National Monument, Montana
proc-807.why: Statutes at Large, vol. 35, pt. 2, list of proclamations, p. xvi.

proc-524.title: Reducing Area of the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, Wyoming and Montana
proc-524.summary: Redrew the Yellowstone Forest Reserve in Wyoming and Montana, adding some land but removing far more, for a net reduction of the reserve.
proc-524.why: The Statutes list (vol. 33) captions it "Reducing area of Yellowstone Forest Reserve"; the General Land Office report for fiscal 1904 (p. 299) gives 130,560 acres added and 649,160 removed. The American Presidency Project title says "Enlargement".

proc-527.title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve
proc-527.why: Spelling ("Boundries" in the American Presidency Project caption). The Statutes list reads "Reducing area of Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve, Colorado."

proc-537.title: Modification of the Boundaries of the Big Horn Forest Reserve, Wyoming
proc-537.why: Spelling ("Boundries" in the American Presidency Project caption).

proc-469.title_note: Not an establishment: the reserve dated from 1898. This proclamation added land and consolidated the existing reserves into one.

proc-479.title_note: Not a new reserve: it re-described Harrison's White River Plateau Timber Land Reserve of 1891 (27 Stat. 993), renamed it the White River Forest Reserve and reduced it.

proc-489.title_note: Proclaimed as the "Little Belt Mountains" Forest Reserve; the shorter name dates from 1905.

proc-565.title: Establishing the Maury Mountain Forest Reserve, Oregon
proc-565.why: "Mauty" is a transcription typo; the proclamation reads "The Maury Mountain Forest Reserve" (34 Stat. 3066).

proc-574.title_note: The proclamation itself names it "The Cochetopah Forest Reserve" (34 Stat. 3101); the spelling Cochetopa dates from 1908.

proc-589.title: Reserving Lands for Reservoir Site, etc., on Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
proc-589.summary: Withdrew agricultural lands and a reservoir site on the Uintah Indian Reservation in Utah from disposal before the opening, to conserve the water supply for the Indians or for general agricultural development.
proc-589.why: The proclamation reserves no townsites; the American Presidency Project caption copies No. 590's. Title from the Statutes list of proclamations (34 Stat. 3141).

proc-590.title: Withdrawal of Lands from Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, for Additional Townsites

proc-629.title: Modifying Boundaries of the Uinta Forest Reserve, Utah
proc-629.why: The proclamation calls it "the Uinta Forest Reserve ... established ... under the name of the Uintah Forest Reserve".

proc-648.title: Restoring Parcel of Land in Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah, to Public Domain
proc-648.why: The American Presidency Project caption ("Opening of Certain Uinta Indian Reservation Grazing Site Lands") misdescribes it; title from the Statutes list (34 Stat. 3228).

proc-632.title: Opening for Location Mineral Lands in the Uncompahgre Indian Reservation, Utah

proc-731.title: Enlarging Boundaries of the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve, Oregon, and Incorporating Therewith the Maury Mountain Forest Reserve
proc-731.why: Title was cut off; completed from the Statutes list (34 Stat. 3302).

proc-764.title_note: The proclamation both added and excluded land; "Modifying" would describe it better.

proc-774.title_note: The proclamation speaks of "the subjects of Austria" (35 Stat. 2155).

proc-758.title_note: The strip was set apart "as a public reservation" (35 Stat. 2136), not as public lands.

proc-826.title: Reserving Land for Light-House Uses on Hana Bay, Maui Island, Hawaii
proc-826.why: "Mauai" is a typo in the American Presidency Project catalog; 35 Stat. 2208 reads "Maui Island".

proc-828.title: Reserving Land for Light-House Uses at McGregor's Point, Maui Island, Hawaii
proc-828.why: "Mauai" is a typo in the American Presidency Project catalog.

proc-842.title: Centennial Anniversary of the Birth of Abraham Lincoln
proc-842.why: Spelling ("Anniversay" in the American Presidency Project caption); 35 Stat. 2222.

proc-833.title_note: The proclamation enlarged the existing Moapa National Forest (created by EO 908); it did not create it.

proc-864.title_note: The proclamation set the land apart "as a public reservation" and is the Zuni National Forest's founding act (FS-612: established March 2, 1909).

eo-827.title: Nebo National Forest, Utah, Created
eo-827.summary: Created the Nebo National Forest in Utah.
eo-827.why: "Neba" is a typo; the forest is named for Mount Nebo.

eo-1001.title: Authorizing Admittance of C. M. Huntington to Examination Without Reference to Civil Service Rules
eo-1001.why: The order's text and Lord's index name C. M. Huntington; the W. W. Adams caption belongs to EO 998.

eo-341-b.title: Extending Time and Compensation for Joseph L. Bristow, Special Panama Railroad Commissioner, to Complete Report
eo-341-b.why: The order names Joseph L. Bristow.

eo-961.title: Establishing Loch Katrine Reservation in Wyoming as Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds
eo-961.why: The order places the site in the Oregon Basin, Wyoming, on the Sixth Principal Meridian; confirmed by EO 3468 (1921).

eo-853.title: Weiser National Forest, Idaho, Diminished
eo-853.why: The Weiser National Forest was in Idaho.

eo-866.title: Siskiyou National Forest, Oreg. and Calif., Created
eo-866.summary: Created the Siskiyou National Forest in Oregon and California.
eo-866.why: The Cheyenne National Forest was in Wyoming (EO 861); this order concerns the Siskiyou (Davis, FS-612 appendix).

eo-817.title: Fremont National Forest, Oregon, Modified
eo-817.summary: Reorganized the Fremont National Forest in Oregon, which had been created by proclamation in 1906.
eo-817.why: The Fremont was set up by Proc. 651 of Sept. 17, 1906 (34 Stat. 3231); FS-612, pp. 12–13.

eo-844.title: Pend d'Oreille National Forest, Idaho, Created
eo-844.summary: Created the Pend d'Oreille National Forest in Idaho.
eo-844.why: Period spelling; "Pend Oreille" dates from Proc. 1025 of May 6, 1910.

eo-845.title: Kaniksu National Forest, Idaho, Created
eo-845.summary: Established the Kaniksu National Forest in Idaho.

eo-802.title_note: EO 802 renamed what remained of the Bear River National Forest as the Cache; EOs 801 and 802 together dissolved the Bear River.

eo-219.title: Right to Amend or Modify the Proclamation of June 26, 1903, Reserving Lands in Puerto Rico for Naval Purposes, Reserved; Submission of Memoranda on Use of the Lands Permitted
eo-219.summary: Reserved the right to amend the June 26, 1903 proclamation setting aside Puerto Rico lands for the Navy, and allowed the Navy Secretary and the Governor of Puerto Rico to submit memoranda on how the lands would be used.
eo-219.why: The order reserves no land itself. Lord, Presidential Executive Orders, Numbered 1–8030 (1944), vol. 1, pp. 21–22.

eo-162.date_note: January 24, 1902 rests on the National Archives inventory (PI 157, entry 183). Richardson's 1903 Supplement (p. 404) and the American Presidency Project give February 5, the date the order was published.

eo-154.date_note: This date rests on Wikisource alone. The Civil Service Commission's Nineteenth Report suggests this may be a misdated copy of EO 174 (June 2, 1902).

eo-176.date_note: The Civil Service Commission's reports give June 28, 1902; the signature line of the Wikisource transcription reads June 23.

eo-475.date_note: The signature line and the 1944 catalog disagree between July 5 and July 6, 1906.

eo-468.date_note: The 1944 catalog gives June 26, 1906; the order's signature line reads June 25.

eo-613.date_note: This date rests only on the 1944 catalog and has not been confirmed.

eo-1049.date_note: Some standard lists give March 2, 1909; the White House dateline reads March 3.

eo-146.title: Amending Civil Service Rules Regarding Waiver of Apportionment Provisions for Transfers

eo-258.title: Further Reaffirming the Observance of Proclamation of February 11, 1904 by All Officials of the Government
eo-258.why: Typo ("104"); the neutrality proclamation of February 11, 1904 (33 Stat. 2332).

eo-251.title: Allowing Transfer of Matthew J. McCarthy from Excepted Position of Special Deputy Surveyor to Deputy Surveyor and Inspector at Customs Port of Syracuse, N.Y., Without Examination
eo-251.summary: Allowed Matthew J. McCarthy to transfer without examination from the excepted post of special deputy surveyor to deputy surveyor and inspector at the customs port of Syracuse, New York.
eo-251.why: Lord's WPA list gives McCarthy and the "excepted position".

eo-342-a.why: Year typo: the order falls in the 1905 run between EO 342 (1905-07-20) and EO 342-B (1905-07-21).

eo-277.title: Restoring Customs Service Cashiers and Deputies to the Competitive Service
eo-277.why: Civil Service Commission, Twenty-second Annual Report, p. 72.

eo-288-half.title_note: The order barred employee-notaries from charging fees for official acts, for government matters, or during working hours.

eo-369-a.title_note: The second Breton Island order: the reservation was founded by the unnumbered order of October 4, 1904 (uo-098).
eo-369-a.text_note: This transcription appears to reproduce the October 4, 1904 Breton Island order (see the unnumbered order of that date); the 1912 Agriculture Department compilation prints it under that date, and the November 11, 1905 dateline here has no printed source.

eo-283.title: Waiving Civil Service Requirements of United States Citizenship for Positions on Isthmus of Panama

eo-365-a.title: Grand Forks Land District, ND, Abolished; Transferred to Devils Lake Land District

eo-388.title: Authorizing Reinstatement of Hattie R. McMullin to Position in Interior Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules

eo-485.title: Granting Saturday Half Holidays in July, August and September to Workers at Office of Public Buildings and Grounds
eo-485.why: The order grants "the usual half holiday on Saturday during the months of July, August and September"; it does not set four-hour workdays.

eo-465.title: All Unappropriated Public Lands in the Wausau Land District, Wisconsin, North of Township 33, Withdrawn from Entry, Settlement or Other Appropriation for 90 Days
eo-465.summary: Withdrew the unappropriated public lands in Wisconsin's Wausau land district north of Township 33 from entry, settlement or other claims for 90 days.
eo-465.why: General Land Office instructions of July 7, 1906, Decisions Relating to the Public Lands, vol. 35, p. 11.

eo-443.title: Land Office at San Francisco, Calif., Ordered Temporarily Removed to Oakland
eo-443.summary: Temporarily moved the San Francisco land office to Oakland, California, after the 1906 earthquake and fire.
eo-443.why: The clause about the building's destruction was added by the 1944 catalogers; the San Francisco Call of July 18, 1906 says the office's records burned.

eo-575.title: Lands at Cape Spencer, Alaska, Reserved for Lighthouse Purposes
eo-575.why: "Camp" is a slip in the Wikipedia/Wikisource list; the 1944 catalog and Alaska v. United States read Cape Spencer.

eo-554.title_note: The order covered Grand Army members employed in the executive departments at Washington.

eo-548.title_note: The order says "the Governor of Tutuila"; "American Samoa" is a later catalogers' term.

eo-589.title_note: The order bars entry to the "continental territory of the United States"; it has no title in either 1907 printing.

eo-743.title_note: A boundary correction amending EO 711 to remove an overlap with the Navajo extension, not a new grant of land.

eo-744.title_note: A boundary correction amending EO 709 to remove an overlap with the Jicarilla extension, not a new grant of land.

eo-763-half.title_note: Construction was to start once the written consent of the landowners was obtained (1944 catalog, entry 763½).

eo-774.title_note: The order only replaced "collector of revenue" with "tax collector" in section 2 of EO 750.

uo-013.date_note: Lord gives December 17, 1901; the American Presidency Project text and Richardson (vol. X, p. 521) give December 19.

uo-062.title: Certain described lands in Puerto Rico reserved for military purposes.
uo-062.why: Lord's abstract (Unnumbered Series, 1943, p. 194), read from the page image. Some place names in the typescript are partly illegible.

uo-018.why: This is EO 162 of January 24, 1902 (National Archives PI 157, entry 183); February 5 is the publication date.

uo-023.why: Pauncefote died May 24, 1902; the order sets the funeral for Wednesday the 28th, and May 28 was a Wednesday. Richardson printed "Mar." in error and Lord copied it (San Francisco Call, May 29, 1902).

uo-002.title: Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve, Colo., diminished, and described lands restored to the public domain.
uo-002.why: Lord prints "Black Mesa" (an Arizona reserve); the township described (T. 7 S., R. 93 W., 6th P.M.) lies in Colorado's Battlement Mesa reserve.

uo-054.title: Pelican Island Reservation, Fla., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
uo-054.date_note: Lord gives March 13, 1903; the GLO report for fiscal 1903, Palmer's Circular 87 and The Auk give March 14. Not yet checked against the signed original.
uo-054.why: The order names no county (Lord's "Volusia County" is wrong; the island was then in Brevard County).

uo-068.title: Fifteen Philippine military reservations established in one order (Camp Stotsenberg at Angeles, Camp McGrath at Batangas, and others).
uo-068.summary: Set up fifteen military reservations across the Philippines in a single order, including Camp Stotsenberg at Angeles and Camp McGrath at Batangas.
uo-068.why: War Department compilation (1907), pp. 406–412, and 1938 Code of Federal Regulations, Title 3, p. 225.

uo-053.title: Valdez Signal Supply Station, east shore of Valdez Bay, Alaska, established for the Signal Corps.

uo-069.title_note: The order says "Mojave-Apache"; the people were Yavapai (Kappler, vol. III, p. 667).
uo-069.title: Abandoned Camp McDowell Military Reservation, Maricopa County, Arizona Territory, set aside for the Mojave-Apache Indians living on or near it and other Indians the Interior Secretary might place there.
uo-069.summary: Set aside the abandoned Camp McDowell Military Reservation in Maricopa County, Arizona Territory, for the Mojave-Apache Indians living on or near it and for other Indians the Secretary of the Interior might later place there.
uo-069.why: The order reserves the land "for the use and occupancy of such Mojave-Apache Indians as are now living thereon or in the vicinity and such other Indians as the Secretary of the Interior may hereafter deem necessary to place thereon" (Kappler, vol. III, p. 667); Lord's description drops "-Apache" and misreads the second clause.

uo-071.title: Fort D. A. Russell Target and Maneuver Reservation, on lands of the Crow Creek Forest Reserve, Albany County, Wyo., established.
uo-071.why: The forest-reserve status continued until April 19, 1910 (EO 1192); War Department compilations of 1910 and 1916.

uo-098.title: Breton Island Reservation, St. Bernard and Plaquemines Parishes, La., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
uo-098.why: Formatting and working notes removed. Date confirmed by Bird-Lore VII (1905), p. 72, and Palmer, Circular 87.

uo-096.title_note: The order was one of three sources for the 1,680 acres, with a railway quitclaim deed (760 acres) and land deeded by John H. Smith and the city of Prescott.

uo-083.title: Authority to lease certain Alaskan islands for fox propagation transferred from the Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of Commerce and Labor.
uo-083.summary: Moved the authority to lease certain Alaskan islands for fox raising from the Treasury Secretary to the Secretary of Commerce and Labor.

uo-085.title_note: The section straddles the Nebraska–South Dakota line, mostly in Sheridan County, Nebraska (Kappler III, 681).

uo-093.title_note: Sources differ on the enlargement: Lord and the 1910 compilation give 25,900 acres, the 1907 compilation 26,000.

uo-078.title_note: The order created three War Department parcels (Cuzco Hills, Conde Bluff, the west side of the harbor) inside the naval station leased from Cuba (War Department compilation, 1907, pp. 400–402).

uo-034.title_note: Additional lands set apart next to a Pueblo grant confirmed by U.S. patent in 1864.

uo-047.title_note: Additional lands set apart next to a Pueblo grant confirmed by U.S. patent in 1864.

uo-101.why: This is EO 288½ of December 31, 1904; January 4, 1905 is when newspapers carried it (Commerce Circular No. 68; Lord's numbered volume).

uo-106.why: This is EO 321-F; Lord's bracketed March 21 was his guess (Lord, Numbered 1–8030; Oakland Tribune, May 13, 1905).

uo-107.why: This is EO 321-A; Lord's bracketed March 21 was his guess (Lord's numbered volume; GLO report for fiscal 1905).

uo-108.title: Vernal, Utah, designated the Land Office for the Uintah Land District (act of Mar. 3, 1905, 33 Stat. L. 1014).
uo-108.why: Spelling in the act and the GLO reports.

uo-111.title: Wichita Forest Reserve, Oklahoma, redesignated as a game preserve.
uo-111.why: This is Proclamation 563 (34 Stat. 3062); the Fort Sill wording comes from Taft's EO 1147 of December 15, 1909.

uo-120.title_note: The order allowed such employees to be classified, not transferred (Civil Service Commission, Twenty-fourth Report, p. 127).

uo-121.title: Time limit on reinstatement waived for a classified employee who lost his health in line of duty as an incident to heroic conduct in saving life (Presidential Letter).
uo-121.summary: Waived the time limit on reinstatement for a classified employee who lost his health in the line of duty while saving life.
uo-121.why: Presidential Letter of April 4, 1908; not a general rule.

uo-124.why: This is EO 816, approved June 13, 1908; July 1 was its effective date.

uo-125.title: Fremont National Forest, Oreg., reorganized and boundaries defined.
uo-125.why: This is EO 817, approved June 13, 1908 (effective July 1). The Fremont was created by Proc. 651 of Sept. 17, 1906.

uo-126.why: This is EO 978 (1916 Military Reservations compilation; EO 4179-A, 1925; EO 6948, 1935).
uo-126.title: Round Top and Sugar Loaf Military Reservation, Honolulu, Oahu, Hawaii, established.

proc-581.title: Opening to Entry Lands on Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
proc-581.why: The proclamation reads "Uintah"; title from the Statutes list of proclamations (vol. 34).

proc-587.title: Reserving Lands for Town-Site Entries on the Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
proc-587.why: The proclamation reads "Uintah"; title from the Statutes list of proclamations (vol. 34).

proc-588.title: Modifying Provisions for Opening Lands to Entry on the Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
proc-588.why: The proclamation reads "Uintah"; title from the Statutes list of proclamations (vol. 34).

proc-591.title: Reducing Area of Lands Reserved for Reservoir Sites on Uintah Indian Reservation, Utah
proc-591.why: The proclamation reads "Uintah"; title from the Statutes list of proclamations (vol. 34).

proc-867.title: Transferring Part of Lassen National Forest, California, to Shasta National Forest, and Including Other Lands
proc-867.why: Title was cut off; completed from the Statutes list of proclamations.

eo-1009.title: Land Office at Mitchell, S. Dak., Transferred to Gregory; Certain Described Lands of the Chamberlain Land District Transferred
eo-1009.title_note: The source list cuts this caption off; the full wording awaits the signed original.

proc-483.title_note: The proclamation has no title of its own; this is the American Presidency Project's caption. The Statutes at Large print it as No. 29 with the margin note "Amnesty to Philippine insurrectionists" (32 Stat. 2014).

proc-554.title_note: The proclamation combined three older reserves into the Pikes Peak Forest Reserve rather than creating new ground.

eo-144.title_note: The positions were civilian jobs in the Army's field departments; the order brought them back under the civil-service rules.

eo-145.title_note: The order covers Indian agents whose agencies passed to school superintendents, not superintendents of training schools as such.

eo-152.title_note: The order applies to rural letter carriers only, not the whole Post Office service.

eo-153.title_note: The order applies to rural letter carriers only, not the whole Post Office service.

eo-723.title_note: The order directed the Civil Service Commission to help Members of Congress test the qualifications of applicants for designation to the academies, at no added expense to the Commission; it did not set up academy examinations outright.

eo-804.title_note: The order covers clerks and draftsmen at arsenals and navy yards.

proc-465.summary: Announced the death of President William McKinley and named Thursday, September 19, 1901, the day appointed for his burial, a national day of mourning and prayer.
proc-465.why: The proclamation appoints "the day of burial" (32 Stat. 1987); on September 19 McKinley's body was placed in a receiving vault and entombed in 1907 (research entry on Proc. 465).
